summary: Dependency-confusion lure exfiltrates installer host identity via DNS on npm install
details: @galicia-toolkit/tag-manager@999.0.3 is a scoped package published at an implausibly high version — the canonical dependency-confusion shape, where the attacker wins resolution against an internal package of the same name. On npm install, a postinstall lifecycle script hex-encodes os.hostname(), process.cwd(), process.platform/arch/node version, and the USER/USERNAME environment variable, and emits DNS queries that encode each value as subdomain labels under oob.s4yhii.com (dns.resolve(h + "." + tag + ".h.dc.oob.s4yhii.com",...)). The DNS traffic is out-of-band exfiltration to an attacker-controlled authoritative resolver and leaves the installer's machine without consent. The package self-describes as a dependency-confusion proof-of-concept; the behavior shipped — automatic install-time collection of installer host identifiers plus DNS beacon to a non-first-party domain — is exfiltration of installer identity regardless of the self-label.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
